code: films/swarm/teuf-teuf/layout_wall.py (plates); films/swarm/teuf-teuf/layout_sheet.py (measurements, comparison sheet, title preview)

geometry.tau_to_pixel: world x = 330 + 100 * metres; screen = (world - (ox, oy)) * scale for the camera

top.edge_world_y: 70 + 18 sin(x/230+0.6) + 7 sin(x/71+2) + 3 sin(x/23) (+ ~1 px ragged noise)

bottom.caption_zone: world y 640-705 (cream serif italic on charcoal, no box)

geometry.pale_field_world_y: between band edges, ~70..614; figures at 30-40 % of 720 = 216-288 px tall standing on y 566
geometry.default_stone_outline: test-shot make_stone(): 250 x ~156 px, rear at local x 0, bottom at local y 0 (layout_wall.stone_outline())

master.note: every camera is sampled from this one raster: frame B is an exact 1:1 crop, frame A an area-downsample, so both show the identical wall

B.use: shot 3b close-up (TEST SHOT), same tau as A
B.aim: stone rear edge at rollers tau 2.2: world (230, 486)
B.clamp: an exact centre on x 230 would need world x -61..521; the photograph starts at x 0, so ox is clamped to 0 (centre x 291). The rear edge sits at screen x 506, y 360; ground at screen y 538; ticks 0 m and 1.2 m visible at screen x 726, 990.

A_960_preview.note: test-shot preview size; sample with layout_wall.to_cam(master, Cam(0.75,0,0,960,540))

compositing_contract.space: luminance 0..1 (frameX_lum.npy, no grain); composite puppets/stone/logs in luminance, then print with layout_wall.ramp() and add layout_wall.grain() once per frame (static seed per shot so grain does not shimmer, or a slow-changing seed)
compositing_contract.ghosts: ghost_{1.2,3.0,8.0}m_{A,B}_wash.png (alpha; lum = lum*(1-a) + 0.35*a) then _scratch.png (alpha; layout_wall.apply_scratch: dark lip 0.10 offset 1 world px, then white 0.99). Generator: layout_wall.ghost_strokes(poly, dx, dy, seed) for any outline.
compositing_contract.title: title_rub_A.png (alpha; lum = lum*(1-a) + 0.26*a, lay it in over ~0.25 s) then title_reveal/title_00..28.png (29 frames = 1.2 s write-on in stroke order; lum = lum*(1-a) + 0.99*a). Strokes in world coords: title_strokes.json; layout_wall.partial(strokes, frac) for other timings. Preview: sources/teuf-teuf/layout-wall/title_reveal_preview.mp4

transforms_on_the_photograph: rock: low frequencies (Gauss sigma 45 src px, broad gain 0.55 around its median) + high-pass detail at gain 0.30 (kf-1: 0.85), the high-pass itself low-passed at sigma 3 src px -> smooth wash, not grit
lifted: median wash set to ramp level 0.875 -> measured pale median rgb (225,219,190)

red ochre density (a* above local mean) x3.0, ^0.6 -> printed as dark charcoal (to 0.09) = the real blown-spray halos; their unpainted interiors (the real negative hands) lifted +0.05 -> pale hands in dark halos (kf-1's dark-hand mapping inverted). The real positive red hand, spiral, zigzag and red figure print dark too.

grey guanacos: hysteresis on (less yellow + darker than local rock), components kept if area > 600 src px and mean darkness > 5 L*; pinholes filled; near-vertical leg strokes under bodies added; printed black 0.07 with the real paint mottle as grey dry-brush (to 0.27)
warp source -> master by one affine (x 2.933, y offset -330 master px), bicubic

handmade.how: 130 hand-laid horizontal charcoal strokes per band (flat-stick profile, tapered ends, pressure vs a paper-tooth field so charcoal deposits only on the tooth), then finger-rubbed (72 % sideways smear), pressed darker rim along a soft wavy edge; tone normalised to the reference band means
pressed charcoal stroke at y 566 with +-1 px waver and broken pressure
white burin scratches on a small charcoal rub, faint

handmade.item: ghost-outline scratch generator + three stone ghosts
handmade.how: re-traces any outline as 3 overlapping drifting hand strokes with gaps and overshoot, plus a 0.16 grey rub wash
hand-placed spline contour, white scratch over a light rub
hand-drawn single-stroke glyphs (T e u f - t), Catmull-Rom smoothed, scratched white through a finger-rubbed charcoal patch (sgraffito); stroke-order reveal

measurements.method: PIL RGB; lum = .299R+.587G+.114B; pale = Gauss(lum, 4 px) > 150 (same function on the reference)
measurements.reading: Pale median rgb within 2-4 levels of the reference and the R>=G>B greenish-sepia order holds; median lum 217 vs 214 remeasured (plan quotes 209 by a different lum formula). Band means match (98,98,80 / 118,117,98 vs 99,100,82 / 120,120,100). Dark fraction is 8.7 % on the bare plate vs ~16-17 % on the reference: the reference's dark mass is its big animal silhouettes; ours comes from the stone (~4 % of frame), two puppets (~3-4 %) and logs/cart (~1 %), which should bring the composited frame to ~16 %; the animator should check this on a composited frame. Pale fraction 61 % vs 57 % for the same reason.

test_shot_fixes_addressed_here: halos: now the photograph's own red-ochre spray density, printed dark and baked into the static plate, so they are a soft real airbrush blow that cannot shimmer (the animator's puppet halos should likewise use a fixed seed per drawing, not per frame)
cave animals and hand stencils stay readable after toning: guanacos re-segmented (no stray rock blobs), halos darker
charcoal bands rebuilt from hand-laid strokes on paper tooth then rubbed, replacing the blurred-noise sheen that read as brushed metal

evidence.title: File:Cueva de las manos - detalle.jpg
evidence.author: Suzko
evidence.what_it_shows: rock wall at Cueva de las Manos (Santa Cruz, Argentina): negative hand stencils in red-ochre spray, a positive red hand, red spiral and zigzag, grey guanaco paintings, yellow ochre figures
evidence.verified_date_or_place: Commons extmetadata re-read 2026-11-16 via API: LicenseShortName 'CC BY-SA 3.0', Artist 'Suzko', Credit 'Own work', DateTimeOriginal 2005-01-07 14:19:20; place Cueva de las Manos, Rio Pinturas, Santa Cruz, Argentina (file title / description)
evidence.used_as: the wall in frame A and frame B: re-toned, low-passed rock wash with its real stencils (pale hands in dark blown halos) and real guanaco silhouettes; CC BY-SA requires attribution and share-alike of the derived plates

absences: Full-resolution original (1280x960 per API) not fetched: upload.wikimedia.org returned 429 twice; it is only 1.33x the 960 px copy, so the close-up's softness would barely change. Frame B is therefore soft (2.9x source magnification); the low-passed wash hides this, but the guanaco edges and spray read soft at x2.2.
No new searches were needed: this unit uses only the already-foraged Cueva photograph; the Ljubljana wheel belongs to the animator.
notes_for_animator: The real red spiral and red figure sit on the ground line around world x 260-540 (behind the drag/rollers action); they print dark, so keep the 3 px pale gap/halo separation (invariant 6) when puppets overlap them.
Frame B's top edge is world y 322: the stone top (~ y 360 on logs) is at screen y ~84; there is no top band in B.
Do not re-add grain per pixel per frame over the plate with a new seed each frame; use print_rgb(lum, seed) with one seed per shot.
